iterations.thought: The origin's time budget names the lever without ambiguity: read 126.7 s and transfer 188.1 s are FULLY SERIAL (29.3 + 43.5 = 72.8 ms/block vs 73.2 measured), the device is idle-waiting (sync_wait 0.06 pct), and the transfer runs at the pageable PCIe rate. Two independent levers attack that, and the method file ranks overlap (tier 3) and cheaper bytes (tier 2/4) above tuning, so I take both and I take them SEPARATELY so the attribution is per-lever: C2a --readahead moves the pread onto a producer thread, which should collapse the wall to max(read, transfer) = 43.5 ms/block; C2b --h2d register page-locks the pool, which removes the staging copy and should both speed the transfer to 40.2 ms/block AND make it truly asynchronous; C2c is both. whole-job recorded readahead and register as ANTI-COMBINING, but it priced that against a per-process wall where the cudaHostRegister pin fee was charged to the measurement -- in this campaign the pin happens before the window opens and the metric excludes it, so that finding does not transfer and C2c is worth measuring rather than assuming. A second reason to expect register to matter beyond speed: the entire 9 pct noise floor lives in the pageable path, so page-locking may buy REPRODUCIBILITY as well as throughput, and a lower floor is what lets every later iteration resolve smaller effects. In parallel and declared as PIPELINING, one implementer builds the bf16-on-the-wire path for iteration 3, because halving the wire bytes is the only lever that moves the one-card ceiling from 8004 GB to the read plateau at 10992 GB. Its one load-bearing constraint, which I gave it as a requirement rather than leaving to discovery: the f32->bf16 cast must be ROUND-TO-NEAREST-EVEN, because truncation is a biased error of ~2^-9 toward zero that lands sigma_max ~2e-3 low and fails gate G1's 1e-4 threshold by ~20x, while RNE is unbiased and should put G1 near 1e-5.

iterations.thought: Iteration 5 left exactly one hypothesis standing and one measurement that would settle it, so iteration 6 makes that measurement instead of guessing. The claim to test is that the champion's 8.05 GB of host pools are backed by 4 KiB pages while the probe's ~2 GiB pool gets 2 MiB huge pages, under a 74 pct compaction failure rate -- and that the difference is worth 12.5 GB/s of read bandwidth because an 8 MiB O_DIRECT read becomes a 2048-entry scatter-gather list instead of a 4-entry one. TWO INDEPENDENT PROBES, either of which can refute it. (a) THE CLIFF: run the iteration-1 standalone reader probe unchanged except for pool size, at roughly 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 GiB. If the mechanism is real there is a CLIFF, not a slope, and it sits where the allocator stops granting huge pages; if the probe reads 36.9 GB/s at 16 GiB the hypothesis is dead and the difference is the CUDA context or the pinning, not the size. (b) THE DIRECT READ: AnonHugePages from /proc/self/smaps for the pool's own address range, printed by the harness itself, on both a probe and a champion. That converts the mechanism from inferred to measured or kills it. IN PARALLEL, THE FIX THAT FOLLOWS IF IT IS REAL: an implementer makes the pool ask for huge pages explicitly (madvise MADV_HUGEPAGE, and MAP_POPULATE so the faulting happens once at setup while the request can still be satisfied, both of which land outside the steady window by construction) and reports the region's AnonHugePages in the STEADY5 row so every future row carries its own evidence.
